mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening consumer demand offset by a construction rebound, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as cyclical equities benefit from the sector rotation.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls > 2% YoY and HOUST rises > 5% MoM
regime_hint: late-cycle demand deceleration with sector rotation
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive (> 0%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 4% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing corporate margins and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% over three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of higher inflation and tighter policy, which increases risk premia and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: high inflation and restrictive policy regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average while consumption (GDPC1) stagnates signals a precautionary savings regime, which reduces near-term consumption-sensitive spending and depresses cyclicals, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12mo MA for 6 consecutive months and GDPC1 flat (< 0.2% MoM)
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% month-over-month while the unemployment rate remains below 4% signals an overheating labor market, which accelerates wage growth and input costs, ultimately eroding margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 1% MoM and UNRATE < 4% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the housing starts index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a sustained contraction in residential construction activity, which reduces demand for building materials and related equities, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
